description: Run about 24,000 commercial customer VMs on 13 commercial hypervisor clusters and storage arrays at DC-1, DC-2, and DC-3; console access; snapshots; paid replication
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: 99.95% monthly SLA: any outage over about 22 minutes in a month triggers the 10% credit tier, and about 7.3 hours triggers 25%; 38 banks' 4-hour notification threshold (12 CFR 53.4); RPO 15 minutes applies to the paid replication tier (about 35% of VMs). Other customers' data recovery depends on their own or the company's backup service
manual_workaround: Fail replicated VMs over to the other data centers; restore unreplicated VMs from the backup service (BP-08) or customers' own backups; NOC posts status updates every 30 minutes
dependent_third_parties: DC-1, DC-2, DC-3 colocation providers; upstream carriers; hardware maintenance vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Platform engineers; NOC; data center operations managers and cages at DC-1, DC-2, DC-3
quantified_operational_impact: About 1,850 customers and 24,000 VMs; DC-1 alone holds about 13,000 VMs (54%)
quantified_regulatory_impact: Bank notice duty for 38 banks after 4 hours of material disruption; MSA breach across many customers

description: Run about 2,100 VMs for 7 federal agencies and 19 defense contractors on the 3 government clusters at DC-2 and DC-3, with all VMs replicated between the two sites
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Agency mission systems run on these VMs; 99.95% SLA in the agency terms; loss of agency confidence affects FedRAMP reuse; every government VM is replicated, so RPO is 15 minutes for all
manual_workaround: Fail over to the paired government cluster at the other data center; agencies run their own continuity plans for longer outages
dependent_third_parties: DC-2 and DC-3 colocation providers; upstream carriers
dependent_people_or_facilities: Platform engineers with government cluster access (U.S. persons); NOC
quantified_operational_impact: About 2,100 VMs; 7 agencies and 19 defense contractors
quantified_regulatory_impact: Agency contract terms; availability incidents must appear in the FedRAMP availability reporting service (CDS-CSO-AVR, Class C, from 2027)

business_process: Control plane and customer portal (commercial partition)
description: Self-service provisioning, VM power and console, DNS changes, public API, and metering for commercial customers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Running VMs keep running without the control plane, so the MTD is longer than hosting. After a business day customers cannot scale or recover and support volume exceeds NOC capacity. RPO 1 hour limits lost orders and DNS changes. The only restore test (2025) took 9 hours (gap 8)
manual_workaround: NOC performs urgent VM power actions in the hypervisor managers on ticket request; engineers make urgent DNS changes on request
dependent_third_parties: Public cloud provider; code hosting vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Control plane engineers; site reliability; NOC
quantified_operational_impact: About 15,000 commercial portal users; about 9,000 API calls a minute at peak
quantified_regulatory_impact: Portal SLA 99.9%; credits on portal fees

business_process: Control plane and customer portal (government partition)
description: Provisioning, VM power and console, and API for agency and defense users, with federal credential sign-in
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Same reasoning as BP-03. Restore tested quarterly and last met the 4-hour RTO in 2026-06
manual_workaround: NOC performs urgent VM power actions in the government hypervisor managers through PAM on ticket request
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-02 (government partition); SYS-04 (government account); SYS-03; SYS-06
dependent_third_parties: Public cloud provider (regions under its own FedRAMP certification)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Control plane engineers with government access; NOC
quantified_regulatory_impact: Agency contract terms; FedRAMP availability reporting from 2027

description: Authoritative DNS for hosted domains, internet routing, firewalls, and DDoS scrubbing for all three data centers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Nothing hosted is reachable without DNS and routing, so this outage counts against every customer's SLA at once; bank 4-hour threshold
manual_workaround: Secondary DNS at the scrubbing service and at a second data center; second carrier per site
dependent_third_parties: DDoS scrubbing service; upstream carriers (2 per site); domain registrar
quantified_regulatory_impact: Bank notice duty; SLA breach across all customers

business_process: 24x7 NOC, status page, and customer support
description: Monitor the platform, open and work incidents, post status updates, answer customer calls and tickets, send bank and customer notices
process_owner: Director of NOC and Customer Support
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The NOC is the first responder and the channel for customer, bank, and agency communication; a NOC outage during an incident can miss the bank notice duty
manual_workaround: Secondary NOC desk at the DC-2 metro office; NOC staff can work remotely with company laptops; status page runs on a separate provider
dependent_third_parties: Status page provider; telephony provider; ticketing SaaS vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: 118 NOC and support staff in two locations
quantified_operational_impact: About 2,600 tickets and 900 calls a week
quantified_regulatory_impact: Bank notice duty depends on NOC notices; agency notice terms

business_process: Managed services delivery through the RMM tool
description: Patch, monitor, and administer about 11,200 customer servers for 410 customers through the RMM tool
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customer servers keep running without the RMM tool. After any compromise the tool must be validated before it is trusted again (P08), so a fast restore of a compromised tool would spread harm
manual_workaround: Customers use their own remote access for urgent work; engineers patch critical servers manually through customer VPNs on request
dependent_third_parties: RMM vendor; customers' own remote access
quantified_operational_impact: About 11,200 servers; about 35,000 patch jobs a month
quantified_regulatory_impact: MSA credits; bank customers among the 410

description: Run nightly and hourly backup jobs for 620 customers, keep immutable copies, and perform customer restores and DR failovers
process_owner: Director of Backup and DR Services
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Banks and other customers depend on restores after their own incidents; backup copies are immutable, so the backup catalog (RPO 1 hour) is the data at risk, not the copies
manual_workaround: Restore from the other backup site's replica catalog; prioritize bank and agency restore requests
dependent_third_parties: DC-2 and DC-3 colocation providers; backup software vendor support
quantified_operational_impact: 620 customers; about 4.8 PB; about 140 restore requests a week
quantified_regulatory_impact: Banks' own recovery duties depend on the service; MSA credits

description: Build, test, sign, and release the control plane, portal, and VM templates
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Releases can pause for days; security fixes for the control plane cannot. After a pipeline compromise, the pipeline must be validated before use (P08)
manual_workaround: Two-person emergency build from a clean workstation with HSM-backed signing for government templates
dependent_third_parties: Code hosting vendor; public cloud provider
quantified_regulatory_impact: Significant change rules (FedRAMP SCN) for releases to the government partition

description: Collect and analyze logs, triage alerts with the MDR partner, run incident response, and report incidents
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Detection gaps let an attack spread. EDR keeps blocking and the MDR partner keeps watching EDR during a SIEM outage. The FedRAMP 1-hour Initial Incident Report clock (Class C, PAIN-3 to PAIN-5) needs working detection
manual_workaround: EDR console and cloud-native alerts go directly to the on-call SOC analyst; MDR partner watches EDR
dependent_systems: SYS-11; SYS-03; SYS-04 (security tooling and log archive accounts)
dependent_third_parties: SIEM vendor; MDR partner; EDR vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: 22 security and GRC staff; MDR partner
quantified_regulatory_impact: FedRAMP incident reporting (IEC rules from 2027-01-01); bank and DFARS reporting depend on detection

business_process: FedRAMP continuous monitoring and agency reporting
description: Produce monthly continuous monitoring deliverables (scans, inventory, POA&M), answer agency requests, and keep the certification package current
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Monthly deliverables can slip a few days without loss of certification; repeated misses would. From 2027 the rules move to Ongoing Certification Reports every 3 months and monthly vulnerability reports
manual_workaround: Assemble deliverables from scanner and CMDB exports by hand
dependent_third_parties: FedRAMP Recognized independent assessment service; legacy secure repository
quantified_regulatory_impact: FedRAMP certification maintenance; agency ATO conditions

description: Quote, contract, and onboard new customers and services; verify customer administrators
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: New business can wait several days; existing customers are unaffected
manual_workaround: Paper or emailed order forms; manual provisioning by engineers for urgent orders

description: Collect usage from the control plane, invoice monthly, and collect payments
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Invoices are monthly; metering data is held in the control plane with RPO 1 hour, so billing can catch up
manual_workaround: Invoice from the prior month's usage and true up later

description: Biweekly payroll, onboarding, terminations, and background checks
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Missed payroll has legal and retention effects; terminations must still remove access on time
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll through the payroll provider; manual termination checklist to Corporate IT
quantified_operational_impact: 600 employees paid biweekly; about 6 terminations a month

business_process: Corporate IT, email, chat, and collaboration
description: Workforce identity, email, chat, file sharing, and endpoint management that every team uses
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Staff can work from phones and the out-of-band channel for a day; incident coordination needs a working channel
manual_workaround: Out-of-band messaging group on company phones; printed call trees in each office and data center
dependent_third_parties: Productivity suite vendor; identity provider vendor
quantified_regulatory_impact: None directly; supports every notice process

description: Remote hands, cage access, hardware replacement, and spares at DC-1, DC-2, and DC-3
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Failed hardware lowers cluster capacity; clusters run with N+1 capacity for about a day
manual_workaround: Colocation remote hands under existing tickets; spares stocked at each site
dependent_third_parties: DC-1, DC-2, DC-3 colocation providers; hardware maintenance vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Data center operations managers and platform engineers
quantified_regulatory_impact: Colocation access lists are a FedRAMP physical control for the government cages
